description: Render a post as each destination platform will show it — WITHOUT creating anything. Nothing is written, scheduled or published; call create_post afterwards with the same arguments to actually post it. Takes the same arguments as create_post (caption, hashtags, accountIds, mediaIds, type, thread, replyTo, quote, audio, collaborators, reelCover, trialReel), and returns the same preview a client with MCP Apps renders as an interactive card, one tab per platform. Use this before create_post whenever the user is composing rather than dictating: it is the cheapest way to show them what goes out, and it reports what would be rejected or silently dropped — a caption over the tightest platform's budget, a platform that requires media when there is none, a thread longer than the strictest limit, audio on a platform with no music API, Instagram collaborators on an account that cannot invite them, a reel cover or trial on a post that is not a reel (or a cover create_post would refuse), media Bluesky leaves behind (it takes up to four images or one video), and X's own rules — more than one $cashtag in a post, a thread reply @mentioning somebody new to the conversation, the same post on two X accounts, a reply or quote X only takes from an account the target post names, media X leaves behind. The character counts it returns are per platform and authoritative: they are the same ones create_post enforces. For Pinterest, include board (and link/title) too — the preview warns when a Pinterest target has no board, which is the way a Pinterest post most often fails. The board name is taken as given: create_post checks it against the account's boards (see list_boards) and refuses an unknown one before writing anything. A preview reads only this workspace's own accounts and media and calls no social network, so nothing outside Ravenpost is touched or shown to anyone.

audio.description: Instagram reel track, for the preview caption line

board.description: Pinterest board name or id — pass it so the preview does not warn about a board you already picked

collaborators.description: Instagram co-author usernames, as you would pass them to create_post. Nothing in the card draws them — pass them so the preview can warn when the targeted Instagram accounts cannot invite them and they would be dropped.

hashtags.description: Hashtags to append to the caption (with or without a leading #)

link.description: Facebook link card / Pinterest pin destination URL

mediaIds.description: Ordered media asset ids (from upload_media / list_media)

quote.description: X quote: tweet id or URL to embed as a card — X only takes it when that post is the account's own or @mentions it

reelCover.description: Instagram reel cover, as you would pass it to create_post — checked against the media library the way create_post checks it, and drawn on the card.

mediaId.description: A JPEG from the media library — an id from list_media or upload_media (which writes JPEG) — 8 MB at most. 9:16 fits: Instagram shows its middle 9:16 in the Reels tab and its middle square on the profile grid.

offsetMs.description: Or a frame of the reel itself: milliseconds from the start of the video (2500 = 2.5 s), before it ends.

replyTo.description: X reply: tweet id or URL the head post replies to — X only takes it when that post is the account's own or @mentions it

thread.description: Follow-up posts, previewed as the reply chain they publish as

trialReel.description: Instagram trial reel graduation, as you would pass it to create_post.

workspaceId.description: Which workspace to act in — an id from list_workspaces. Optional with a single workspace; REQUIRED once there are several, where guessing would mean posting one client's content to another client's accounts. Ask the user which one before publishing.

name: preview_post
title: Preview a post
